title: Distributed Request Fingerprint and Context-Bridging Hub
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: create a small, deterministic request fingerprint and a lightweight context-bridging hub that SDKs and edge middleware can emit/normalize. This ticket unifies cross-transport request identity and provides a low-cost path for correlating traces and logs across HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket/worker queues without forcing explicit trace context in every hop. The feature should enable: 1) robust correlation for partial or sampled traces, 2) opportunistic replay of context for background workers, and 3) consistent routing for debug/backfill pipelines.

Background: we currently have many incompatible carriers (X-RW-Trace, X-Request-ID, legacy vendor headers) and worker-queue metadata which causes missed correlations and noisy dashboards. Prior tickets implemented transport-specific shims; this work builds a convergent id and bridging hub that: - SDKs emit a compact fingerprint header when one doesn't exist, - edge/middleware normalize and translate diverse incoming carriers into the canonical header, - internal proxies and workers can attach a stable fingerprint into logs/metrics for later stitching.

Design highlights and constraints: - Fingerprint must be deterministic and stable for the life of a logical request but cheap to compute (no network calls). - Header size target: <= 32 bytes (base64/hex short string). - Privacy: never include raw PII. Use a salted hash with deployment-local salt; salts are rotated via KMS-managed secrets outside this ticket. - Backward compatibility: if a full traceparent/trace-id exists, fingerprint should be derived from it (stable mapping) to avoid split traces. If no trace context, fall back to hashed (service+path+short-timestamp-bucket+randomized nonce). - Performance budget: microbenchmark must show <0.05ms median added latency on typical request path and <0.1ms p99 in cold path. - Sampling and sampling alignment: fingerprint will be used to bucket requests for thin-client sampling hints (not to override backend samplers), enabling sampling alignment across services when the policy is enabled.

Implementation plan: 1) Spec and RFC (this ticket) -> 2) Go/node/python SDK changes to compute emit header X-RW-FPR (opt-in via SDK config flag defaulting to enabled for internal teams) -> 3) edge proxy (ingress) adapter normalizes incoming carriers into X-RW-FPR -> 4) runtime sidecar/proxy ensures worker queue metadata contains fingerprint field -> 5) tracing backend mapping and ingestion changes to accept fingerprint as an alternate correlation key; logs/metrics pipeline updated to index it.

Trade-offs considered: - HMAC vs plain hash: HMAC protects against collision attacks but requires key management; we chose salted SHA256 truncated then base62-encode to keep size small and avoid secret rotation complexity in initial rollout. We documented migration to HMAC as a follow-up. - Deterministic mapping from trace-id vs generating new: mapping preserves continuity for requests already sampled; generating new provides coverage for unsampled beginnings. We derive from trace-id when present, otherwise generate.

Open questions: - Should ingress adapters canonicalize legacy vendor headers to our header name, or only map them into internal metadata? (current plan: ingress writes canonical header and emits legacy-preserve tag in logs) - Salt rotation schedule and rollout blinding: operations will handle; we need a short runbook for backwards stitching when salts change.

Acceptance criteria:
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (go/node/python) emit X-RW-FPR header for outgoing requests when enabled and attach fingerprint to internal request context.
Ingress adapter normalizes at least the following carriers into X-RW-FPR: Traceparent/trace-id, X-Request-ID, X-RW-Trace, legacy vendor-id headers.
Microbenchmarks show median added latency <0.05ms and p99 <0.1ms for fingerprint computation in SDK hot path.
No plaintext PII is present in header values; all fingerprints are deterministic, salted hashes that cannot be reversed.
Tracing backend and logs pipeline can join on X-RW-FPR for test dataset (internal tracing test harness) and stitching rate improves by >=20% in flaky path scenarios.
Feature gated rollout plan exists: feature flag for SDK, canary ingress rollout, and a rollback strategy.
Documentation and SDK changelog published and an internal runbook for salt rotation and incident steps created.
End-to-end integration test that simulates HTTP -> queue -> worker shows preserved fingerprint and correlated spans/logs.
Observability dashboard tile added: fingerprint adoption rate, unique fingerprints per minute, stitch success rate, and fingerprint-origin breakdown (derived-from-trace vs generated).

2026-03-04 - Miguel Santos: PoC in node-sdk branch 'fpr-poc' created: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/3287. Initial microbenchmarks look promising (~25us median).
2026-03-05 - QA: Added integration test harness that replays 10k synthetic traces through HTTP -> SQS -> worker and validates stitch rate.
2026-03-06 - Design review (J. Lee): recommended reducing header entropy to 20 bytes to save space in some proxies. We adjusted to 20-byte truncated SHA256 base62.
2026-03-07 - Security (R. Kumar): confirmed salted-hash approach acceptable for initial rollout; recommended explicit KMS-backed HMAC follow-up ticket for high-risk customers.
2026-03-09 - Miguel Santos: Implemented ingress normalization in nginx sidecar config + envoy filter prototype; performance regression under 0.5% at 10k rps during canary tests.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created rollout checklist and canary plan; target teams: payments, search, and console-beta. Schedule set for 2026-03-15 canary window.
Code review notes: prefer deterministic fallback ordering (trace-id -> x-request-id -> generated) and explicit instrumentation points in SDK request wrapper.
